capabilities.title: True and false query constants
limitations: No high-level Rust, Python, or TypeScript facade helper currently constructs these constants.

capabilities.title: Comparison queries
limitations: The Python and TypeScript q facades do not yet expose comparison constructors.

capabilities.title: Range queries
limitations: The Python and TypeScript q facades do not yet expose range constructors.

capabilities.title: Phrase queries
limitations: The TypeScript high-level q namespace does not yet expose a phrase helper.

capabilities.title: sameElement query
limitations: Requires supported array-of-struct fields and native elementFilter; it is not a general nested struct or map model. The Rust query helper exists, but the current high-level Rust schema facade cannot itself define the required array-of-struct field.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: Fuzzy query
limitations: The TypeScript high-level q facade does not yet expose a fuzzy helper.

capabilities.title: Prefix, suffix, and substring queries
limitations: the Python and TypeScript q facades do not yet expose

capabilities.title: Alternatives queries
limitations: Alternatives currently executes only when every child is a term; general alternatives are rejected by the adapter. High-level Rust, Python, and TypeScript facades do not expose this node.

capabilities.title: Nearest-neighbor vector search
limitations: The proven public path uses dense tensor query inputs and exposes only target hits, approximate mode, distance threshold, and explore-additional-hits rather than the full Vespa HNSW tuning surface.

capabilities.title: Geo-location and bounding-box queries
limitations: Real Vespa execution is verified, including inclusive bounding-box edges. The high-level schema facades do not yet expose position fields, so geo is not an end-to-end schema-and-query ergonomic SDK capability.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: Predicate queries
limitations: Only the supported predicate feature/range representation and documented expression shapes are lowered. Predicate field definitions are not exposed by the high-level Rust or Python schema facades.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: WeakAnd and WAND queries
limitations: The Python and TypeScript q facades do not yet expose

capabilities.title: Weighted-set and dot-product queries
limitations: The Python and TypeScript q facades do not yet expose weighted-set or dot-product helpers.

capabilities.title: Equivalence queries
limitations: No high-level Rust, Python, or TypeScript facade helper currently constructs equivalence queries.

capabilities.title: Rank query composition
limitations: The TypeScript q facade does not yet expose rank composition.

capabilities.title: userInput and userQuery text parsing
limitations: The parser intentionally supports only a reduced grammar; full Vespa escaping, boosts, range syntax, parser modes, and unsupported composites are rejected. No high-level facade currently exposes userInput/userQuery constructors.

capabilities.title: Structured filters
limitations: The Python high-level facade currently uses textual filters; it does not expose a typed structured-filter helper namespace.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: Textual filter expressions
limitations: The filter expression language is a deliberate subset and is parsed and bound before entering canonical IR. The Rust SearchBuilder currently accepts typed Filter values only; it has no public textual-filter overload.

capabilities.title: Field sorting
limitations: The native hit ABI supports executing field sorts but does not expose Vespa sort values, so public Hit.sort_values is not populated by the real backend.

capabilities.title: First/last missing-value sort placement
limitations: Python and TypeScript high-level sort() helpers

capabilities.title: Limit and offset pagination
limitations: Python additionally exposes page() as a convenience. Rust currently exposes limit/offset but no page() helper.

capabilities.title: Text search-field selection
limitations: Field selection executes, but non-default per-field weights are rejected by the current native adapter. The Python high-level SearchBuilder does not yet expose search_field/search_fields.

capabilities.title: Document-summary field projection
limitations: Stored scalar fields are projected through the current native summary seam. Named summary-class selection, rich docsum value decoding, and summary-feature readback are tracked separately.

capabilities.title: Named summary-class selection
limitations: The public E2E proves default summary selection and field projection only. Native schema generation does not install application-defined named DocumentSummaryDefinition classes, so custom named summary execution is not yet available.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: Rich document-summary values (scalar subset)
limitations: Only scalar string, number, and boolean docsum values are executable through the current native result seam. Arrays, structs/maps, tensors, and other rich Vespa docsum values are not decoded faithfully.

capabilities.title: Summary-feature readback
limitations: Rust, Python, and TypeScript preserve canonical summary-feature values when they are present in a portable or scripted Hit, but the current native adapter leaves summary_features empty instead of decoding native summary-feature values.
Rank-feature projection is likewise preserved when present, but the current native adapter does not populate rank_features.

capabilities.title: Highlighting
limitations: This pass supports Vespa-generated dynamic teaser output for stored, indexed text fields. The TypeScript SearchBuilder does not expose highlighting controls. Custom document-summary definitions, arbitrary Juniper rendering controls, grouped highlights, and rich docsum values remain separate capabilities.

capabilities.title: Dense tensor document readback
limitations: Dense tensor fields round-trip through document GET/projection and reopen. Sparse/mixed document tensors are outside the supported high-level path; Python currently exposes readback as the tagged $searchkernel_tensor object rather than reconstructing a Tensor instance.

capabilities.title: Typed tensor feature readback
limitations: Tensor-backed match features currently cross the native result seam as opaque data bytes. The adapter does not decode them into a portable TensorValue.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: Structured grouping and faceting
limitations: The native lowering is a linear grouping plan and cannot execute arbitrary parallel grouping branches from the full portable tree.

capabilities.title: Executable grouping expression/function subset
limitations: The native adapter supports attributes, literals, arithmetic, aggregation references, aliases, and the verified function subset. Member, MapLookup, and Bucket remain rejected. Rust's public GroupingExpression currently exposes attributes only; Python exposes the richer expression facade.

capabilities.title: Grouping aggregations
limitations: The native layer supports count, average, sum, min, max, stddev, xor, and quantiles. Rust's high-level GroupingAggregation exposes count/average/sum/min/max; Python additionally exposes stddev. Summary aggregation is tracked separately because its hit payload is not complete.

capabilities.title: Summary aggregation
limitations: The native grouping skeleton preserves summary() and finite max propagation, and the Python and TypeScript facades can construct agg.summary(), but grouped docsum payloads do not cross the native ABI. The Python E2E keeps this case explicitly blocked. Rust's current GroupingAggregation facade has no summary variant.

capabilities.title: Grouping continuations
limitations: Continuation tokens are preserved in GroupingRequestIr and in the portable result tree, but native grouping lowering rejects any request with continuations. Python and TypeScript result objects preserve tokens if received, yet there is no production native round-trip or high-level continuation request helper.

capabilities.title: Raw grouping source
limitations: Raw grouping text is represented as caller intent, but resolve_grouping rejects it until a parser/normalizer can produce canonical structured grouping IR.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: Document insert, upsert, patch, delete, and get
limitations: This row covers the ordinary unconditional operations and Patch set/unset. Conditional mutations and advanced update-operation families are tracked separately. Ordered multiple updates targeting the same field are represented by Vespa's model but currently return Unsupported because the portable IR does not yet preserve that ordered field-update sequence.

capabilities.title: Arithmetic document updates
limitations: Increment, decrement, multiply, and divide execute through canonical FlatBuffers -> IR -> native DocumentUpdate in Python. The high-level Rust product API currently has Patch set/unset only and no advanced UpdateBuilder.

capabilities.title: Create-if-nonexistent document updates
limitations: Python UpdateBuilder.create() is proven through the real native path. The high-level Rust product API does not yet expose advanced document updates.

capabilities.title: Conditional document mutations
limitations: Conditions are preserved in canonical IR for upsert/delete/update, but the Vespa adapter returns conditional_mutation_not_supported. Python and TypeScript expose condition arguments/builders; Rust does not.

capabilities.title: Collection add/remove updates
limitations: AddUpdate and RemoveUpdate are represented in FlatBuffers, but update_to_ir currently rejects them as update_operation_not_supported before canonical IR.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: Matched-element updates
limitations: MatchUpdate is represented in FlatBuffers, but the current UpdateOperationIr has no matched-element variant and update_to_ir rejects it before canonical IR.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: Tensor modify updates
limitations: TensorModifyUpdate is represented in FlatBuffers, but there is no tensor-modify UpdateOperationIr and update_to_ir rejects it before canonical IR.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: Dense tensor document values
limitations: Sparse and mixed tensors remain unsupported in the current high-level document and query-input paths.

capabilities.title: YQL query source
limitations: Only the existing low-level parser subset is supported; full Vespa YQL grammar, query profiles, and search chains are outside the embedded wrapper. The public Rust Index has search()/browse() but no yql() entry point.

capabilities.title: Analyzed text search with default WeakAnd semantics
limitations: Primary search(text) is analyzed text retrieval with Vespa WeakAnd-style default matching; it is not a phrase query. The low-level QueryText node is broader than the current facade helpers.

capabilities.title: Typed analyzed-text query nodes
limitations: The typed QueryText node executes through the adapter, but no high-level Rust, Python, or TypeScript q facade helper constructs it.

capabilities.title: Native in-term queries
limitations: The Python and TypeScript q facades do not yet expose

capabilities.title: NonEmpty query wrapper
limitations: NonEmpty validates its lowered child and rejects statically empty boolean operators; it does not reproduce every parser-generated empty marker. No high-level facade helper exists yet.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: Labeled query rank properties
limitations: Labels are allocated by the adapter and exported as internal vespa.label.* rank properties; callers must not provide those properties. No high-level labeled-query helper exists yet.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: Document-summary schema definitions
limitations: Document-summary definitions and fields survive FlatBuffers-to-IR semantic conversion, but native schema generation does not install named document summaries for execution.
The TypeScript facade does not expose this capability as an ergonomic helper; generated low-level FlatBuffers remain available.

capabilities.title: Array-of-struct document fields
limitations: The portable/native path supports the existing array<object> shape used by SameElement. The high-level Rust Field, Python field-spec, and TypeScript schema facades expose only primitive/tensor kinds today; nested structs, maps, and heterogeneous object members remain unsupported.

capabilities.title: Position fields and derived geo attributes
limitations: The native adapter publishes Vespa-compatible derived zcurve data and real geo queries are verified. Position is not exposed by the high-level Rust, Python, or TypeScript schema builders.

capabilities.title: Rank-profile selection
limitations: The profile must exist in the compiled index schema; Search Kernel does not introduce a second ranking language.

capabilities.title: Numeric scalar query inputs
limitations: The public Rust QueryInputValue currently exposes integer, unsigned integer, float, and tensor values; the proven scalar real-engine path is numeric. Expression query inputs are not exposed by the high-level facades.

capabilities.title: Dense tensor query inputs
limitations: Only literal dense tensors are executable by the current native query-input seam; sparse/mixed tensors and expression inputs are rejected.

capabilities.title: Rank properties
limitations: Adapter-owned vespa.label.* properties are reserved for labeled queries and cannot be supplied by callers.

capabilities.title: Match-feature readback
limitations: Scalar native match features are decoded. Rust, Python, and TypeScript preserve typed canonical match, summary, and rank feature maps when those values are present in a portable Hit. Tensor-backed native match-feature output remains opaque bytes, and the native adapter currently leaves summary_features and rank_features unpopulated.

capabilities.title: Recursive grouping result trees
limitations: The canonical IR/result protocol is a heterogeneous recursive ResultNode tree. Rust now preserves nested Hit children with the same Hit decoder used at the root, but its GroupingResult convenience separates nested groups and hits into distinct vectors and does not expose the canonical mixed-child ordering or canonical root directly.

capabilities.title: Coverage and degradation metadata
limitations: The real backend populates coverage counters and match-phase/timeout/ANN degradation flags. Portable timing, trace, arbitrary metadata, and native Vespa UniqueIssues are not currently populated by this backend; UniqueIssues are deliberately not fabricated into SearchResult.errors.

capabilities.title: Embedded single-node Vespa scope
limitations: Distributed routing, configuration services, schema deployment, federation, and other container-level Vespa facilities are outside this wrapper.

capabilities.title: Targeted multi-index daemon lifecycle protocol
limitations: The direct targeted request-envelope and create/open wire contract is the #848 forward-compatibility baseline, but daemon registry/data-root execution lands in #846. Target-less envelopes remain valid only for embedded/per-index callers.
